newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey President signs decree to ease car imports.
newsitem.headline: Turkey President signs decree to ease car imports.

text.p: Turkish President Suleyman Demirel signed a cabinet decree on Thursday to allow duty-free imports of used cars, the Anatolian news agency said.

Under the new scheme, some three million expatriate Turkish workers in Europe will be able to import cars and machinery of up to four years of age without customs duties, if they deposit at least 50,000 marks ($32,850) for one year at state owned Ziraat Bank.
Demirel also signed another decree which will allow a 20 percent reduction in taxes on domestic car purchases by expatriates who make the required deposits.

Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's coalition government had been seeking Demirel's approval for the decree since early September, as part of the coalition's two revenue raising packages to fight huge deficits.

But Turkey's car sector, already harmed by surging imports and slack domestic demand, faces an additional threat from the decree, which was subjected to strong protests from car makers as well as allied industry and labour unions in the automotive sector.
The government forecasts duty free imports of 25,000 cars and an income of 1.3 billion marks from the one-year accounts.
Demirel's press office said the President discussed concerns raised by the automotive industry with the government before signing the decree, the agency reported.

The press office said the government revised the decree slightly by saying expatriates who open the required accounts by end-1996 would be allowed to bring in limited duty-free car imports from June 1, 1997 insteady of January 1.

Turkey's car output slumped by 26 percent from a year ago to 18,540 in September. Nine-month car output was 155,614, down three percent from the same 1995 period while total motor vehicle production firmed nine percent to 237,384.
